title: Steve Brown joins and the Whiteman stage repertoire
summary: He recommended Steve Brown for the band and describes Whiteman's stage show of Rhapsody in Blue, Chloe and the 1812 Overture.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: And then there's Jimmy and Tommy and Bix and Steve. Oh, by this time I had talked to Paul, "How about Steve? I think he'd be good in the band." Steve wasn't the best reader in the world and for all the faking he did, who knows what you're going to do if he played the tune often enough, he's got the part pretty well figured out. But to bow, things like that, which maybe that required, Mike Trafficante was playing the fiddle then, switched over to tuba and that would allow -- Steve also played tuba so the two of them played, things like "1812 Overture" and then Steve played the fiddle. But see, there's all these things to play and I think there are only about four numbers that they played. There was "Chloë" that was a record that sold well, I guess.
And there was "Sundown" -- do you remember that tune?

Yes, Jack Fulton sang that and Skin Young sang the "Chloë" and let's see I think there was another number that we did in the beginning, two numbers. One of them I had made an arrangement of. They used two of them, but they were nondescript numbers. They were nice, but nothing had been
done with them. There had been no records made or anything like that. He used them because he liked them.

The rest was stage stuff, you know, you come on with "Rhapsody in Blue," and then I think they did part of something of -- I think they did the Rhapsody in Blue, a piece of cut, you know, and they did that, and then the -- Willie Hall had a spot and the Rhythm Boys had a spot, 20 minutes or so, and then they did "Chloe" and then at the end it was "1812 Overture".
